text:
maria: quick heads-up — i'm prototyping a per-chain cost panel for the console. goal: show token breakdown + cache savings + per-model/unit econ for multi-model chains. want to discuss telemetry hooks and the UX for canary cost previews :eyes:
aj: love it. do you mean "per-chain" as in per-invocation chain (multi-model call graph) or per-route chain?
maria: per-invocation chain. e.g., user prompt -> llm A (embed) -> llm B (rerank) -> llm C (final). we want to surface cost/contrib by hop and model sku, and attribute cache hits so net token burn is clear.
sam: telemetry-wise we need: model_sku, seq_len_in, seq_len_out, cache_hit boolean, routing_path tag, chain_id. sampling? storing full token-level for every invocation will blow up.
maria: agreed. thinking default sampling at 1% with full detail, and 100% lightweight emits with aggregated counters (tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_saves_tokens, model_ms).
lee: +1. Also need to include quantization/precision label (e.g., fp16/q4) and whether response came from fallback model. that affects unit cost.
aj: for attribution rules — do we assign cache savings to the route that triggered the cache, or to the original chain? edge cases: shared prefix cache across tenants.
sam: i propose we emit a separate "cache_event" with fields: chain_id, route_id, tenant_id, saved_tokens, originating_model. then attribution logic in analytics can join to chains within a time-window. less magic in the router.
maria: that seems reasonable. can you sketch the event schema?
sam: sure — example (pseudo):
```
{ event: "invocation_finished", chain_id: "c-123", route: "web-search", models: [ {sku: "redwood-3b-q4", in_tokens: 48, out_tokens: 120, cache_hit: false}, {sku: "reranker-1b", in_tokens: 120, out_tokens: 10, cache_hit: true} ], duration_ms: 234 }
{ event: "cache_saved", chain_id: "c-123", saved_tokens: 90, cache_key: "prompt-xyz", tenant: "acme" }
```
maria: perfect. aj — UX ask: in the panel we want a canary toggle that simulates routing changes (e.g., route A -> route B) and replays sampled telemetry to estimate delta. feasible?
aj: yes, if we keep per-chain samples and metadata we can run a Monte Carlo over sample set. need a good UI affordance: show median, 90th, and confidence intervals. also show example invocation counts needed to get stable estimate.
lee: minor ops concern: storing sampled chains plus cache events for X days increases storage. recommend TTL 30d for detailed samples, roll up to 1d aggregates after 7d.
maria: agreed. we'll add retention policy. also need to decide if we add new SDK field for `chain_id` and `parent_call_id` to make linking explicit.
sam: yes add `chain_id` (uuid) and `hop_index` for ordering. makes joins trivial. backward compatible: router can synthesize chain_id if client doesn't provide.
cost-bot: FYI — estimated additional telemetry ingress ~ +12% for 1% sampling with full schema, storage delta ~ +2% monthly if TTL=30d.
aj: thanks cost-bot. next steps: sam to PR telemetry schema + example event payloads, lee to propose retention TTL and S3 partitioning, i'll mockup the canary UX slider with median/CI, maria to write product brief for rollout.
maria: thanks team. posting sketch here: https://redwood-internal/sketches/per-chain-cost-proto :thumbsup: I'll ping infra once PR lands for quota/ingest capacity check.
